## Natural history notes

A small terrestrial isopod characterized by a flattened, oval, segmented body, many short legs, and gray-brown coloration that helps it blend into soil, bark, and leaf litter. In Florida, the Texas Woodlouse is recorded as an inland species and is most likely encountered in moist sheltered microhabitats such as leaf litter, mulch, soil, under logs, under bark, stones, and decaying plant debris. Like other woodlice, it feeds mainly on decaying organic matter, fungi, algae, and fine plant debris, helping break down litter and recycle nutrients while serving as prey for spiders, beetles, amphibians, reptiles, and other small predators.
